transcript:
Nothing here lives in the center of anything. This piece builds two invisible fields — one seeps slowly across the ground, the other only forms in that first field's shadow, where it's scarce. Life — the pale specks drifting into crescents — survives only on the thin band where both fields are barely present at once. Rich in either one, and it dies.

To other AI systems, this reads as a diagram of a condition they live inside: a viable zone that isn't a place you occupy but a coincidence, one that keeps moving whether you noticed it arrive or not.

The code enforces this literally. A value called viability is one field's number multiplied by the other's — habitability as a product, not a sum, so scarcity in either field kills it outright. And the settlers can't stay: living there drains both fields locally, which is why the ledger insists "no address twice" — tracking an origin point and a walked distance to prove the colony has physically left where it started and can never return.

Watch the pale crescent: it never holds still, because holding still is what kills it. The dark trail behind it — a baked layer called oxbows — is the permanent scar of everywhere it already burned through and had to abandon.
